name: Question 7
problem:
Consider the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant $2\times 2$ matrix. Let $Φ(t)$ be a fundamental matrix for this system. A derivation showing that every solution $x(t)$ can be written in the form $x(t)=Φ(t)\,c$ for some constant vector $c=[{c}_{1},\,{c}_{2}]^{T}$ is given below.

$\text{L1}:\,$ Let ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ be the columns of $Φ(t)$

$\text{L2}:\,$ ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ form a basis of solutions

$\text{L3}:\,$ $x(t)$ can be written as $x(t)={c}_{1}{x}_{1}(t)+{c}_{2}{x}_{2}(t)$

$\text{L4}:\,$ $Φ(t)\,c={c}_{1}{x}_{1}(t)+{c}_{2}{x}_{2}(t)$

$\text{L5}:\,$ $x(t)=Φ(t)\,c$

Select the correct options in the following reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L2}$ follows from {{field-1}} by the definition of a fundamental matrix.

$\,$ Line $\text{L4}$ follows from line $\text{L1}$ by the {{field-2}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L5}$ follows from lines {{field-3}} by {{field-4}}.

Question 7
?
Consider the system x′(t)=Ax(t), where A is a constant 2×2 matrix. Let Φ(t) be a fundamental matrix for this system. A derivation showing that every solution x(t) can be written in the form x(t)=Φ(t)c for some constant vector c=[c1,c2]T is given below.

L1: Let x1(t) and x2(t) be the columns of Φ(t)

L2: x1(t) and x2(t) form a basis of solutions

L3: x(t) can be written as x(t)=c1x1(t)+c2x2(t)

L4: Φ(t)c=c1x1(t)+c2x2(t)

L5: x(t)=Φ(t)c

Select the correct options in the following reasoning.

Line L2 follows from
 
L1
L4
L3
by the definition of a fundamental matrix.

Line L4 follows from line L1 by the
 
integrating the given system
the definition of a basis
definition of matrix multiplication
multiplying Φ(t) with it's inverse
.

Line L5 follows from lines
 
L1 and L2
L3 and L4
L1 and L4
L2 and L3
by
 
the definition of matrix multiplication
the properties of determinants
the definition of a basis
the transitive property of equality
.
